newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-EMERSON TAKES LEAD IN ENGLISH OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-EMERSON TAKES LEAD IN ENGLISH OPEN.

text.p: Unheralded British professional Gary Emerson, more normally found selling equipment over the counter at the club where he works, took a surprising lead in the third round of the English Open on Saturday.

Emerson fired a seven-under-par 65 to edge a stroke in front of a pair of Swedes, 1995 Ryder Cup player Per-Ulrik Johannson and Dennis Edlund, who shot rounds of 64 and 69 respectively at the par-72 Hanbury Manor course.
Emerson's fellow Englishman Roger Chapman, the leader after the first two rounds, could only compile a 71 and dropped back to fourth place two strokes off the lead.

Emerson's round on another day of sharp-shooting at the new Tour venue northeast of London took him to 201, 15 under par. He had four birdies in the first five holes and eight in all with just one bogey to take pole position in his bid for a first tour title at the age of 33.
His best previous effort was to lie a stroke off the lead with nine holes to play in his second event on tour in 1995, the Turespana Masters, before dropping back to finish fifth.
"Having a winning chance in only my second event probably came a bit too early for me," said Emerson.

"Now all I can hope for is to play a shot at a time and keep my nerve. It would be a dream come true to win. On Monday, though, I'll probably have to still be checking my stock in the pro-shop before the next event."
Johansson, 10th in the Ryder Cup table, will boost his chance greatly of a second Cup appearance if he does well in Sunday's final round.
The 30-year-old Swede, who lives not far from the September Ryder Cup venue of Valderrama, has great ambitions to feature there but will not push too hard.

"It's a great goal to play at Valderrama because of where it is and what it was like playing at Oak Hill in 1995," said Johansson, whose six birdies in his first eight holes took him surging up the field.
"But I don't intend to change my schedule or play all the way through the year to get in. I'll hope to make it the way I've planned."
Spain's Jose Maria Olazabal finished eagle-birdie for a 69 to reach six under but looks too far back to add a second title in only his seventh event since returning from a long injury layoff.
European number one Colin Montgomerie was an embittered man after a bad start left him needing a good finish to salvage a 70. He made three birdies in the last five holes.

"I duffed a chip at the first and couldn't get up and down at the second because of another duff, when 99 times out of 100 I would have, and did something similar at the third. One-over after three and that's end of story," he said.
